arxiv-1901-05674.title: Easy to Fool? Testing the Anti-evasion Capabilities of PDF Malware Scanners
arxiv-1901-05674.creator: Saeed Ehteshamifar, Antonio Barresi, Thomas R. Gross, Michael Pradel
arxiv-1901-05674.description: Abstract Abstract Malware scanners try to protect users from opening malicious documents by statically or dynamically analyzing documents. However, malware developers may apply evasions that conceal the maliciousness of a document. Given the variety of existing evasions, systematically assessing the impact of evasions on malware scanners remains an open challenge.

arxiv-2108-12928.title: Mischievous Nominal Constructions in Universal Dependencies
arxiv-2108-12928.creator: Nathan Schneider, Amir Zeldes
arxiv-2108-12928.description: Abstract While the highly multilingual Universal Dependencies (UD) project provides extensive guidelines for clausal structure as well as structure within canonical nominal phrases, a standard treatment is lacking for many “mischievous” nominal phenomena that break the mold. As a result, numerous inconsistencies within and across corpora can be found, even in languages with extensive UD treebanking work, such as English.

arxiv-2305-11430.title: TELeR: A General Taxonomy of LLM Prompts for Benchmarking Complex Tasks
arxiv-2305-11430.creator: Shubhra Kanti Karmaker (“Santu”), Dongji Feng
arxiv-2305-11430.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Shubhra Kanti Karmaker (“Santu”), Dongji Feng. While LLMs have shown great success in understanding and generating text in traditional conversational settings, their potential for performing ill-defined complex tasks is largely under-studied and yet to be benchmarked. However, conducting such benchmarking studies is challenging because of the large variations in LLMs’ performance when different prompt types/styles are used and different degrees of detail are provided in the prompts.

arxiv-2306-09300.title: Exploring Magnetism of Lead-free Halide Double Perovskites: A High-Throughput First-Principles Study
arxiv-2306-09300.creator: Utkarsh Singh, Johan Klarbring, Igor A. Abrikosov, Sergei I. Simak
arxiv-2306-09300.description: Abstract We have performed a comprehensive, first-principles high-throughput study of the magnetic properties of halide double perovskites, C ​ s 2 ​ B ​ B ′ ​ C ​ l 6 Cs_{2}BB^{\prime}Cl_{6} , with magnetic ions occupying one or both B and B ′ sites.

arxiv-2307-16521.title: THERMO-MECHANICAL LEVEL-SET TOPOLOGY OPTIMIZATION OF A LOAD CARRYING BATTERY PACK FOR ELECTRIC AIRCRAFT
arxiv-2307-16521.creator: Alexandre T.R. Guibert 1, Murtaza Bookwala 1, Ashley Cronk 2, Y. Shirley Meng 3, and H. Alicia Kim 1,2
arxiv-2307-16521.description: Abstract A persistent challenge with the development of electric vertical take-off and landing vehicles (eVTOL) to meet flight power and energy demands is the mass of the load and thermal management systems for batteries. One possible strategy to overcome this problem is to employ optimization techniques to obtain a lightweight battery pack while satisfying structural and thermal requirements.

arxiv-2312-06935.title: Time-Scaling, Ergodicity, and Covariance Decay of Interacting Particle Systems
arxiv-2312-06935.creator: Maciej Głuchowski, Georg Menz
arxiv-2312-06935.description: Abstract The main focus of this article is the study of ergodicity of Interacting Particle Systems (IPS). We present a simple lemma showing that scaling time is equivalent to taking the convex combination of the transition matrix of the IPS with the identity. As a consequence, the ergodic properties of IPS are invariant under this transformation.

arxiv-2402-12488.title: Model Predictive Control Design for Unlocking the Energy Flexibility of Heat Pump and Thermal Energy Storage Systems
arxiv-2402-12488.creator: Weihong Tang, Yun Li, Shalika Walker, Tamas Keviczky
arxiv-2402-12488.description: Abstract Heat pump and thermal energy storage (HPTES) systems, which are widely utilized in modern buildings for providing domestic hot water, contribute to a large share of household electricity consumption. With the increasing integration of renewable energy sources (RES) into modern power grids, demand-side management (DSM) becomes crucial for balancing power generation and consumption by adjusting end users’ power consumption.

arxiv-2411-18891.title: Backward Linear-Quadratic Mean Field Stochastic Differential Games: A Direct Method Thanks: This work is supported by National Key R&D Program of China (2022YFA1006104), National Natural Science Foundations of China (12471419, 12271304), and Shandong Provincial Natural Science Foundations (ZR2024ZD3
arxiv-2411-18891.creator: Yu Si, Jingtao Shi
arxiv-2411-18891.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yu Si, Jingtao Shi. Abstract: This paper studies a linear-quadratic mean-field game of stochastic large-population system, where the large-population system satisfies a class of N weakly coupled linear backward stochastic differential equation. Different from the fixed-point approach commonly used to address large population problems, we first directly apply the maximum principle and decoupling techniques to solve a multi-agent problem, obtaining a centralized optimal strategy. Then, by letting N tend to infinity, we establish a decentralized optimal strategy.

arxiv-2502-07551.title: Early Stopping Against Label Noise Without Validation Data
arxiv-2502-07551.creator: Suqin Yuan, Lei Feng, Tongliang Liu
arxiv-2502-07551.description: Abstract Early stopping methods in deep learning face the challenge of balancing the volume of training and validation data, especially in the presence of label noise. Concretely, sparing more data for validation from training data would limit the performance of the learned model, yet insufficient validation data could result in a sub-optimal selection of the desired model.

arxiv-2509-02700.title: Hierarchical assembly impedes the inference of stellar mass growth histories for individual galaxies 2026 Hierarchical assembly impedes the inference of stellar mass growth histories for individual galaxies – 10
arxiv-2509-02700.creator: R. K. Cochrane
arxiv-2509-02700.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by R. K. Cochrane. Some massive, quiescent galaxies at z > 3 z>3 appear to contain considerable numbers of old stars (forming at z > 7 z>7 ). Works inferring the star formation histories of at least one such galaxy observed with JWST have suggested that the assembly of so much stellar mass so early may challenge the well-established Cold Dark Matter (CDM) cosmological framework, or else indicate extraordinarily high past star formation efficiencies.

arxiv-2510-00407.title: Investigating Encoding and Perspective for Augmented Reality Motion Guidance
arxiv-2510-00407.creator: Jade Kandel, Sriya Kasumarthi, Spiros Tsalikis ∗, Chelsea Duppen, Daniel Szafir ∗ Michael Lewek ‡ {\ddagger} Henry Fuchs ∗ Danielle Szafir ∗ University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
arxiv-2510-00407.description: Abstract Augmented reality (AR) offers promising opportunities to support movement-based activities, such as personal training or physical therapy, with real-time, spatially-situated visual cues. While many approaches leverage AR to guide motion, existing design guidelines focus on simple, upper-body movements within the user’s field of view.

arxiv-2512-19069.title: Can abstract concepts from LLM improve SLM performance?
arxiv-2512-19069.creator: Siddharth Tandon
arxiv-2512-19069.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Siddharth Tandon. Large language models (LLMs) excel at diverse tasks, but their deployment on resource-constrained devices remains challenging. Existing methods like quantization, pruning, and distillation can reduce memory footprint but often demand extensive experimentation and careful infrastructure design. Leveraging existing techniques for extracting high-level concepts (represented as steering vectors) from larger models, we investigate their transferability to smaller language models (SLM) during inference.

A detailed connectivity map covering the entire brain would therefore be of great value. Based on diffusion MRI, we propose an efficient methodology to generate large,

pmc-10663835.title: Robust and adaptive terrain classification and gait event detection system
pmc-10663835.creator: Usman Qamar Shaikh, Muhammad Shahzaib, Sadia Shakil, Farrukh A. Bhatti, Malik Aamir Saeed
pmc-10663835.description: Real-time gait event detection (GED) system can be utilized for gait analysis and tracking fitness activities. GED for various types of terrains (e.g., stair-walk, uneven surfaces, etc.) is still an open research problem. This study presents an inertial sensor-based approach for real-time GED system that works for diverse terrains in an uncontrolled environment.

pmc-11393416.title: Novel immunotherapeutics against LGR5 to target multiple cancer types
pmc-11393416.creator: Hung-Chang Chen, Nico Mueller, Katherine Stott, Chrysa Kapeni, Eilidh Rivers, Carolin M Sauer, Flavio Beke, Stephen J Walsh, Nicola Ashman, Louise O’Brien, Amir Rafati Fard, Arman Ghodsinia, Changtai Li, Fadwa Joud, Olivier Giger, Inti Zlobec, Ioana Olan, Sarah J Aitken, Matthew Hoare, Richard Mair,
pmc-11393416.description: We have developed and validated a highly specific, versatile antibody to the extracellular domain of human LGR5 (α-LGR5). α-LGR5 detects LGR5 overexpression in >90% of colorectal cancer (CRC), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and pre-B-ALL tumour cells and was used to generate an Antibody-Drug Conjugate (α-LGR5-ADC), Bispecific T-cell Engager (α-LGR5-BiTE) and Chimeric Antigen Receptor (α-LGR5-CAR).

pmc-11394062.title: Neuroimaging in Nonsyndromic Craniosynostosis: Key Concepts to Unlock Innovation
pmc-11394062.creator: Camilla Russo, Ferdinando Aliberti, Ursula Pia Ferrara, Carmela Russo, Domenico Vincenzo De Gennaro, Adriana Cristofano, Anna Nastro, Domenico Cicala, Pietro Spennato, Mario Quarantelli, Marco Aiello, Andrea Soricelli, Giovanni Smaldone, Nicola Onorini, Lucia De Martino, Stefania Picariello, Stefano
pmc-11394062.description: Craniosynostoses (CRS) are caused by the premature fusion of one or more cranial sutures, with isolated nonsyndromic CRS accounting for most of the clinical manifestations. Such premature suture fusion impacts both skull and brain morphology and involves regions far beyond the immediate area of fusion.

pmc-11480453.title: Interaction of chikungunya virus glycoproteins with macrophage factors controls virion production
pmc-11480453.creator: Zhenlan Yao, Sangeetha Ramachandran, Serina Huang, Erin Kim, Yasaman Jami-Alahmadi, Prashant Kaushal, Mehdi Bouhaddou, James A Wohlschlegel, Melody MH Li
pmc-11480453.description: Despite their role as innate sentinels, macrophages can serve as cellular reservoirs of chikungunya virus (CHIKV), a highly-pathogenic arthropod-borne alphavirus that has caused large outbreaks among human populations. Here, with the use of viral chimeras and evolutionary selection analysis, we define CHIKV glycoproteins E1 and E2 as critical for virion production in THP-1 derived human macrophages.

pmc-11512765.title: The Impact of Traditional Chinese Herbal Decoctions Combined with Rehabilitation Therapy on Pulmonary Function and Respiratory Muscle Strength in COVID-19 Recovery Patients
pmc-11512765.creator: Li Luo, Xi-Jiao Liu, Dong-Ling Chen, Xiao-Ya Deng, Yong-Hong Pan, Sheng Li
pmc-11512765.description: ObjectiveThis study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy of integrated traditional Chinese and Western medicine rehabilitation treatment during the recovery period of COVID-19, providing a scientific basis for developing more effective rehabilitation protocols.MethodsThe study included 120 COVID-19 (novel coronavirus) recovery patients treated at our hospital from November 2021 to April 2022.

pmc-12952195.title: Association of Posttransplant Kidney Function With Patient Reported Outcomes: A Single Center's Experience Over Nearly Two Decades
pmc-12952195.creator: Peter Thorne, Laura A Binari, Scott A Rega, Guneet Kochar, Rachel C Forbes, C Wright Pinson, Irene D Feurer, Beatrice P Concepcion
pmc-12952195.description: BackgroundImpaired kidney function in the non‐transplant chronic kidney disease (CKD) population has been shown to negatively affect patients’ health related quality of life (HRQOL). The relationship between posttransplant graft function, as measured by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and patient‐reported outcomes (PRO) remains poorly understood.

pmc-13079811.title: Study on the influence of stress relief in close-distance coal seam Goaf and roadway excavation disturbance on surrounding rock
pmc-13079811.creator: Zenghui Liu, Minjun Chen
pmc-13079811.description: To investigate the influence of pressure relief in the close-distance coal seam goaf and roadway excavation disturbance on surrounding rock stability, this study focuses on the large-section open-off cut of Ⅱ8224 N. Methods employed include RQD rock mass quality evaluation, FLAC3D numerical simulation, similar material simulation experiments, and field borehole camera observation.

pmc-13100193.title: A dual-branch deep learning framework for emotion recognition from EEG signals
pmc-13100193.creator: Debam Saha, Asfak Ali, Vycheslav Gulvanskii, Dmitrii Kaplun, Ram Sarkar
pmc-13100193.description: Mental health monitoring through emotion recognition plays an important role in early intervention and personalized healthcare systems. Traditional EEG-based emotion recognition approaches have encountered significant limitations, including heavy reliance on manual feature engineering, poor generalization across datasets, and computational complexity that restricts real-world deployment.
